sections.label: CPIB findings on rental
sections.summary: CPIB investigations found no preferential treatment, abuse of position, or conflict of interest, and that rules were followed and proper market rental paid.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The CPIB investigations have made clear that there was no preferential treatment or abuse of position, the rules were followed, proper market rental was paid, and Senior Minister Teo's report also makes clear there was no conflict of interest.

sections.label: Rental offer and acceptance
sections.summary: An agent advised $25,000 a month was fair, SLA counter-offered $26,500, and this was accepted without further negotiations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: My agent advised me that $25,000 a month would be a fair offer, based on rentals for similar properties at that time and taking into account the built-up area and the condition of the property.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) came back with a counter-offer of $26,500, which we accepted without further negotiations.

sections.label: No profit from rentals
sections.summary: The speaker states he is not making money from the rental difference, paying for 26 Ridout Road mostly from renting out his family home, with a net deficit after property and income tax.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But I will add, in fact, the answer is no, I am not making any money from the difference in rentals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I pay for the rental of 26 Ridout Road mostly from renting out my family home, but taking into account, one, property tax because the family home is now non-owner occupied; and two, income tax on the rental proceeds, there is a net deficit.

sections.label: Size of land area
sections.summary: The speaker states he did not want the extra land of about 150,000 square feet now part of the lease.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Next, some have asked about the size of the land area.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I did not want the extra land, about 150,000 square feet, which is now part of the lease.

sections.label: Spending on improvements
sections.summary: The speaker counts more than $500,000 on improvements, including paying for the car porch and planting many trees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Actually, on my count, more than $500,000 on improvements, including paying for the car porch and planting many trees.

sections.label: CPIB review and recusal
sections.summary: CPIB investigation and review found no conflict of interest, no breach of rules, and everyone acted properly and honestly; the speaker took himself out of the matter and made no decision for SLA or MinLaw.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The CPIB investigation and review have made clear that there was no conflict of interest, no breach of rules and everyone acted properly and honestly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Yes, SLA is a Ministry of Law (MinLaw) Statutory Board.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But I took myself completely out of this matter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I have an interest in the tenancy, obviously.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But I made no decision for SLA on the matter, either SLA or MinLaw.

sections.label: Recusal and chain of command
sections.summary: The speaker told Indranee Rajah and a MinLaw Deputy Secretary that he was recusing himself, with Indranee Rajah to handle issues and check with Teo if needed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The then-Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah told me that she would check with Senior Minister Teo if she needed to.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And I told the then-Deputy Secretary at MinLaw that I am recusing myself in this matter, that then-Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah will deal with the issues, if they arise and, if she needed to, she will check with Senior Minister Teo.

sections.label: SLA guidance chain of command
sections.summary: The speaker told his agent that SLA would go to Indranee Rajah and Teo for guidance on any issue, creating a chain of command not involving him.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In this way, there would be a chain of command, which did not involve me, for SLA to check with then-Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah and Senior Minister Teo, if there were issues on which SLA wanted guidance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And I also told my agent that, on this matter, I had spoken with then-Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah and Senior Minister Teo, and if any issue arose, SLA will go to them to check.

sections.label: No issues went for guidance
sections.summary: Nothing went to MinLaw, Indranee Rajah or Teo for guidance or decision, and the speaker says he removed himself completely from decision-making.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Nor in this case, as it transpired, did anything go up to MinLaw, then-Senior Minister of State Indranee Rajah or Senior Minister Teo for guidance or decision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I had removed myself completely from the decision-making process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And no potential or perceived conflict either, because I had recused myself.

sections.label: Recusal removes conflict of interest
sections.summary: The speaker says recusal means he cannot make a decision, so there is no potential or perceived conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If I have an interest and I remain able to make a decision even though I do not actually make any decision, there can be potential or perceived conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But once I recuse myself, I cannot make a decision, nor am I potentially able to make a decision.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I am, like my colleagues, fully committed to working with Singaporeans to address the issues that matter to them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I will answer any questions Members have because it is important that we do the right thing and to hold ourselves up to high standards of integrity.

sections.label: CPIB findings on Ministers
sections.summary: CPIB found no disclosure of privileged information and no preferential treatment given to the Ministers and their spouses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: CPIB subsequently found that there was no disclosure of privileged information and no preferential treatment given to the Ministers and their spouses.

sections.label: CPIB and AGC conclusions
sections.summary: CPIB found no evidence of abuse of position for personal gain or disclosure of privileged information, and the AGC directed no further action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The CPIB looked into the matter and found no evidence to suggest any abuse of position for personal gain.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The CPIB also concluded that there was no disclosure of privileged information in the process of the rental transaction.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The AGC reviewed CPIB's investigation papers, concurred with CPIB's findings and recommendations and directed that no further action be taken as the facts did not disclose any offence.

sections.label: SLA list to company
sections.summary: In June 2019, SLA gave a company a list of state properties it wanted to rent for its employees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: In June 2019, SLA provided a list of several state properties to a company which was looking to rent several properties for its employees for its operations in Singapore.

sections.label: CPIB findings and themes
sections.summary: CPIB did not disclose corruption or criminal wrongdoing, and the questions cover good governance, land management and Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While CPIB did not disclose corruption or criminal wrongdoing, the two themes I will cover in my questions cover good governance and land management and Reserves.

sections.label: Ministerial Code and PAP rules
sections.summary: The question asks how the Senior Minister's report reconciles with the Ministerial Code and PAP Rules of Prudence requiring Ministers to keep official and private affairs separate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How does the Senior Minister's report reconcile this with the Ministerial Code of Conduct and the Prime Minister's Rules of Prudence for the People's Action Party (PAP) Members of Parliament, which requires that all Ministers should scrupulously keep their official and private affairs separate?

sections.label: SLA guide rent and GFA
sections.summary: The question asks whether SLA's guide rent using gross floor area rather than total land area is a policy loophole and special dispensation at taxpayers' expense.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Senior Minister Teo's report is silent on why Minister Shanmugam did not have the confidence of the SLA, a Statutory Board that comes under his Ministry's purview and the Second Minister's purview, in maintaining the adjacent land next to 26 Ridout Road in spite of SLA being prepared to pay up to $25,000 a year for its upkeep.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With SLA choosing to focus almost singularly on gross floor area (GFA) and not total land area in its guide rent of black and white bungalows, including those in the most expensive and prime housing estates comprising GCB, does this not represent a policy loophole that effectively is a special dispensation at the taxpayers' expense, for individuals who can afford to rent black and white bungalows?

sections.label: Black and white bungalow land areas
sections.summary: The question asks the Second Minister for Law to confirm how many of Singapore's 600 black and white colonial bungalows have total land area larger than 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, can I ask the Second Minister for Law also to confirm, of the 600 black and white colonial bungalows in Singapore, how many have the total land area larger than 26 Ridout Road today?

sections.label: SLA valuer and tenant identity
sections.summary: SLA valuers take this into account in valuation, and the SLA valuer did not know the negotiated rental amount or the prospective tenant's identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In the valuation of the property by the valuers of SLA, they take this into account when assigning that valuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I should point out, as I said just now, that the SLA valuer did not know the rental amount which the leasing division had negotiated with the tenant, nor the identity of the prospective tenant.

sections.label: SLA land clearance Dalvey Estate
sections.summary: SLA cleared land at a state property in Dalvey Estate in 2018 to address disamenities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: An example where SLA also cleared land to address disamenities is at a state property in Dalvey Estate in 2018.

sections.label: Mosquito source site clearance
sections.summary: SLA cleared vegetation and created a two-metre buffer; the tenant was not unhappy and rental was not reduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Having confirmed with the National Environment Agency that the heavily vegetated land was, indeed, the source of the mosquitoes, SLA carried out partial site clearance of the vegetated area and created a two-metre buffer to nearby properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Based on the MA's account, I think the tenant was not unhappy about the smaller fenced-in area because he did not have to maintain the vegetated land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was no reduction in rental as the MA's valuation was based mainly on the GFA of the house.

sections.label: Corruption allegations central issue
sections.summary: Edwin Tong addressed scarce land, but the central issue is allegations of corruption, abuse of power and conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The issue of scarce commodity and land and so forth, I think Second Minister Edwin Tong has addressed that and I think he will be happy to address that further, if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But the central issue why we are here today, actually, is to deal with allegations of corruption, abuse of power and conflict of interest.

sections.label: 26 Ridout Road rental ranking
sections.summary: At the 2018 tenancy, $26,500 monthly rental was top three among Black and Whites, and top four at 2021 renewal.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If you look at the table, you will see that at the time the tenancy was entered into for 26 Ridout Road, and that was in 2018, $26,500 as the monthly rental was the top three in all Black and Whites in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2021, when it was renewed, it remained at the top four.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Throughout this period, rental per GFA, throughout, remained higher than the average – right through – for 26 Ridout Road.

sections.label: Rental per square metre comparison
sections.summary: Annex E1 shows 26 Ridout Road's average rental per square metre per month was $30.94, higher than the $29.78 average.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If Members look at Annex E1, and I invite Mr Pritam Singh to look at it when he has some time subsequently, Mr Singh will then see that the point I made about the average rental per square metre per month on an average basis – 26 Ridout Road – was $30.94 and this is higher than the average of all Black and Whites at $29.78.

sections.label: Tenant maintenance cost
sections.summary: The cost was eventually at the tenant's cost, and the tenant subsequently maintained it at $25,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And it was eventually at the tenant's cost.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was also maintained, subsequently, prospectively, by the tenant at $25,000 per year.

sections.label: Ridout Road land transaction factors
sections.summary: The land abuts 24 Ridout Road, is relatively inaccessible, was not monetised for years, and the transaction was arms-length and commercial; SLA agreed to clearance and Minister Shanmugam will clarify his position.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, overall, looking at all these factors and the piece of land in question which abuts the neighbour, 24 Ridout Road, it sounds very big when you mention it in the way that you have done, Mr Singh.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: But it abuts the neighbour, it is relatively inaccessible, there are only a few access points, it is not a common space where otherwise it could be parcelled out and tenanted to another tenant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For many years prior to that, there was no monetisation of that land by SLA.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, when we consider all these factors, take them all into account, I think the Member will see why this was a transaction, as I said in my speech earlier, that was at arms-length, negotiated, commercial and sought to achieve the state's interests as well.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Mr Pritam Singh asked a second question about why Minister Shanmugam has said that he was not confident that the surrounding land would be properly maintained.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: He had offered, through his agent, to maintain this land at his own cost after it was cleared of the overgrown vegetation.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: SLA agreed to this clearance, did what it needed to do to address the health and safety concerns – there were snakes, mosquitoes and fallen trees which I also mentioned – but since this is a reference to what Minister Shanmugam said, I will invite him to clarify his position on this.

sections.label: Potential conflict of interest identified early
sections.summary: The report found a potential conflict of interest, but Minister Shanmugam identified it early and recused himself from decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: In my report, I have found that there was the potential for a conflict of interest to arise, a potential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: However, Minister Shanmugam identified this potential conflict of interest early, beforehand, and took steps to prevent it from actualising.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: He removed himself from the chain of command and recused himself from any decision-making for the matter in question.

sections.label: No breach after recusal
sections.summary: Given the recusal and removal from duty, there is no potential conflict, no perception of conflict, and no breach of the code of conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Given the recusal and removal from duty, there can no longer be any potential conflict, nor does a perception of conflict arise and, therefore, there is no breach of the code of conduct.

sections.label: Prevention of Corruption Act section 27
sections.summary: Section 27 of the Prevention of Corruption Act requires persons to give information, and a breach could lead to up to a year in jail or a $10,000 fine.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I said in my earlier Statement, they read out to me section 27 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, and I think in section 27, caution was in these terms: "Every person required by the Director or any officer to give any information on any subject which it is the duty of the Director or that officer to inquire into under this Act and which it is in his power to give, shall be legally bound to give that information." I think a breach of it could expose you to a penalty of up to a year in jail or a $10,000 fine.

sections.label: Rental rates and market comparison
sections.summary: 31 Ridout Road was renewed in October 2022 for three years with rent increased to $20,000 from $19,000, about 5%, while URA private residential rents rose about 42% and landed properties 35%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The first is regarding the issue of favourable rental rates and whether, as a result of SLA's management of the renewal process as well as of black and white properties, this has arisen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I note that the property at 31 Ridout Road was renewed in October 2022 for three years, with the rent increased to $20,000 from $19,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is about a 5% increase or so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But if we consider the market conditions, which the Minister also spoke about in his speech just now, if we look at the URA private residential rents, that has increased by about 42% during the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And if we just zoom in on landed properties, it has increased by 35%.

sections.label: Direct tenancy and open tender
sections.summary: SLA states state properties should be let through open tender; 31 Ridout Road was on the SPIO website, but 26 Ridout Road was not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The second clarification is in relation to the direct tenancy process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is stated on the SLA website that state properties are supposed to be let out through open tender to ensure the process is fair and transparent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I know that 31 Ridout Road was, indeed, on the SPIO website, but 26 Ridout Road was not.

sections.label: 31 Ridout Road renewal timing
sections.summary: Renewal for 31 Ridout Road was done in the first quarter of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To the Member's point about the movement of the market, if Members were to just pick up the table I gave out earlier and look at the chart, renewal was done for 31 Ridout Road around the early part of 2022, the first quarter.

sections.label: Rental rate at lease signing
sections.summary: Discussions occurred end of 2021 and early 2022, and the URA rental index rate was similar to when the lease was entered into.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But the discussions took place around this period – end of 2021 and early 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And if Members look at the chart that I have produced, this is the URA rental index, you will see that, at that level, at that location, the rate was – if you look at the horizontal lines across – similar to when the lease was entered into.

sections.label: Colliers managed renewal valuation
sections.summary: COVID-19 affected the market in 2021 and 2022, and external professional Colliers managed the renewal with its own expert valuers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And you must bear in mind also that in 2021 and 2022, there was still the COVID-19 overhang over the market at that point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, these are factors that really – I am not a property agent and I am not a real estate expert, but I go back to the first point I made to the Member, which is, this is looked at by an external professional MA – in this case, it was Colliers – which managed the renewal and they have their own inhouse expert valuers and I would not second-guess that.

sections.label: Publicising properties in uptrend market
sections.summary: In an uptrend market with high demand and limited supply, properties should be put out as publicly as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If the market is on its uptrend, there is a lot of demand with limited supply, then I think you want to make sure that you put it out as much as you can, as publicly as you can, so that there is a really big showing of the properties on offer that is being supplied so that the demand can match up with the supply.

sections.label: SLA designation of works process
sections.summary: The question asks what process SLA uses to designate which works are borne by SLA and which by tenants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is the process by which SLA designates what works will be borne by SLA and which works will then be at the tenants' own cost?

sections.label: Livspace appointment allegation denied
sections.summary: The suggestion that Minister Shanmugam's son or Livspace was appointed is scurrilous; works were tendered and Livspace was not appointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The suggestion that Minister Shanmugam's son or his company, Livspace, was appointed – and I think the sting of these allegations is that there is a preference given to this – is completely scurrilous and unwarranted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For both 26 and 31 Ridout Road, the works that were recommended by the consultant was then done and awarded to a contractor through a tender, and Livspace was not an appointed contractor.

sections.label: CPIB finds allegations untrue
sections.summary: The CPIB has established these and other allegations to be untrue.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The CPIB has established these and other allegations to be untrue.

sections.label: Property valuation by professional valuers
sections.summary: The property valuation is done by professional valuers, and the SLA valuer gave a valuation of $26,500 with the additional land cleared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Second, on the valuation of the property, the valuation of the property is done by the professional valuers and I would not second-guess their valuation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And the valuer in SLA was asked what is the valuation of the property with the inclusion of the additional land cleared, and the valuation that was given by the Valuer was $26,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, that is the professional valuation from the professional valuer.

sections.label: Enhanced due diligence on PEPs
sections.summary: Financial regulators require banks to apply enhanced customer due diligence on customers identified to be PEPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Financial regulators require banks to apply enhanced customer due diligence on customers that are identified to be PEPs.

sections.label: Conflict of interest declaration processes
sections.summary: For key transactions such as public tenders and major project awards, processes exist for public officers to declare conflicts of interest upfront.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: For key transactions, especially transactions that involve public tenders and the evaluation and award of major projects, there are already processes for public officers to declare conflicts of interest upfront.

sections.label: Reporting wrongful practice to agency head
sections.summary: An officer is required to report any wrongful practice to the head of his agency even if instructed by his superior not to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: An officer is required to report any wrongful practice to the head of his agency even if he has been instructed by his superior not to do so.

sections.label: Onus on individual to declare
sections.summary: Agency-level checks are only part of the system and do not address the fundamental issue that the onus rests on the individual to declare and recuse himself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I should also point out that the types of checks at the agency level are only part of the system and actually do not address the fundamental issue at hand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And the fundamental issue at hand is that the onus still rests on the individual to declare and recuse himself to prevent a conflict of interest from arising.

sections.label: Rental transaction declarations rules
sections.summary: Rules require rotation, and the Public Service Division is working with Ministries on declarations for rental transactions, with the Prime Minister's Office also looking at it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: They have to be rotated and these are some of the rules that are in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And I mentioned to Members that the Public Service Division is working with relevant Ministries to see how we can implement declarations specifically on rental transactions and the Prime Minister's Office will look at that as well.

sections.label: Ministerial conflict of interest code
sections.summary: The Code of Conduct for Ministers is not law, and para 3.2 states a Minister must never enter transactions where private financial interest might conceivably conflict with public duty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I must say that I find it disappointing that he reduces the issue of conflict of interest into a legal argument.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I mean, in the Code of Conduct for Ministers, it is stated quite clearly at the bottom of the document that the document does not have the force of law and whether there is a breach or not is not justiciable in a Court of law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second clarification on a related point is, if one looks at para 3.2 of the Code of Conduct, it is stated very strictly, "A Minister, therefore, must never enter into any transactions where his private financial interest might even conceivably come into conflict with his public duty".

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, that is what is stated there – never enter into transactions where his financial interest might conceivably come into conflict with his public duty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, does the Senior Minister agree that it might be reasonable to interpret this to mean that actually the Law Minister should not have entered into this transaction with SLA, which is an agency under his charge, or, at the very least, it was imprudent of him to do so?

sections.label: Shanmugam removed himself from duties
sections.summary: Mr Shanmugam removed himself from duties and powers over a private matter, separating the two and removing one factor needed for conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, that is the import of what conflict of interest is about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And Mr Shanmugam took steps to make sure that he removed himself from those duties and powers that he had over a matter which would have been a private matter and, therefore, the two were separated and one of those two factors which must exist for conflict of interest to arise, which is that the person must have powers over that private matter, was removed.

sections.label: Trees cleared at Ridout Road
sections.summary: The question asks how many trees were cleared at 26 Ridout Road and whether the review covered NParks' process and knowledge of the tenant's identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: First, on the clearing of the adjacent land at 26 Ridout Road, I would like to ask how many trees were actually cleared and did the review by Senior Minister Teo look into not just SLA but NParks – as an involved agency – NParks' process to determine the removal of trees, which trees were removed and so on and, most crucially, did NParks know the identity of the prospective tenant in the course of this process.

sections.label: CPIB versus Auditor-General roles
sections.summary: Asking the Auditor-General to comment on code of conduct compliance goes beyond its ambit, and the CPIB is the agency that investigates such matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: To ask the Auditor-General to comment on whether or not the practices were in line with the code of conduct for Ministers, I think goes beyond the ambit of the Auditor-General.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Why do we call in the CPIB and not the Auditor-General?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Because the CPIB is the agency which investigates such matters.

sections.label: No secret list
sections.summary: There is no secret list.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: First of all, there is no secret list.

sections.label: Properties rented at market
sections.summary: The properties are rented out at market, so there is no great benefit from renting them out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Second, the properties are rented out at market and, so, there is no great benefit from being able to rent out these properties.

sections.label: 26 Ridout Road additional bids
sections.summary: The question asks whether SLA solicited additional bids for 26 Ridout Road after refurbishment to test if the price was fair market price.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For 26 Ridout Road, which had only attracted one bid, did SLA not solicit additional bids after the extensive refurbishment was completed to test if the price was still a fair market price?

sections.label: No declaration requirement
sections.summary: There is no requirement today under the Code of Conduct for the type of declarations Ms Poh Li San is talking about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On Ms Poh Li San's second question, there is no requirement today under the Code of Conduct for the type of declarations which she is talking about.

sections.label: Property remains on market
sections.summary: The property remains on the market until the lease is signed and confirmed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To Ms Poh Li San's first question, the property remains on the market until the lease is signed and confirmed.

sections.label: Minister's rental and conflict of interest
sections.summary: Mr Shanmugam told me what he was going to do and I accepted that; I did not approve his rental or take part in any transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Mr Shanmugam told me what he was going to do and I accepted that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I did not approve his rental; I did not take part in any of the transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Subsequently, if it is discovered, or it is alleged that that director had a conflict of interest, it does not preclude the Chairman from convening a disciplinary committee or even sitting on it, unless he was a participant in the actions of that director which resulted in the conflict of interest.

sections.label: No privileged information sought
sections.summary: The key issue is whether the Minister was seeking privileged information, and there was none.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Yes, I thank Mr Dennis Tan for his question because it is an important question.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But the key issue here is, was there privileged information that the Minister was seeking, and was there privileged information that he was trying to obtain?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And so, I think the key issue here is that there was none.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was no privileged information that the Minister was seeking to obtain.

sections.label: Clarification on Codes spirit
sections.summary: Speaker clarifies an earlier remark that the spirit, not the letter, of the Codes should be observed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I thought I should make a clarification on something I had just said, which my colleagues said may possibly be misunderstood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I had earlier said that it is important to observe the spirit, rather than the letter of the Codes.

sections.label: Minister personal request of civil servant
sections.summary: A question asks Senior Minister Teo whether a Minister may personally request a civil servant about transactions if no privileged information is sought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To Senior Minister Teo, does Senior Minister Teo think that as long as no privileged information is asked for, a Minister can make a personal request of a civil servant relating to transactions under his Ministry?

sections.label: SLA agent asking for Minister
sections.summary: The speaker says an agent asking SLA must be a credible prospect and would name Minister K Shanmugam.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When an agent goes and asks SLA, SLA will ask, "Who are you asking for?" They are not just going to give it to every agent.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I did say, in my understanding, the person who is asking has got to be a credible prospect.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the agent will then say, "It is Minister K Shanmugam".

sections.label: Telling Deputy Secretary transparency interest
sections.summary: The speaker says the context was clear when he told the Deputy Secretary this was in the interest of transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As to whether I told the Deputy Secretary that this is in the interest of transparency, I think the context was clear, because he told me, if I recall correctly, that he will keep the Permanent Secretary informed.

sections.label: Ridout Road no verifiable conflicts
sections.summary: The speaker says the report and statements show no actual or verifiable conflicts of interest in the Ridout Road transactions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, my question on this particular theme is very much in the spirit of this question.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And I understand from the report and the statements made that there were no actual or verifiable conflicts of interest in the Ridout Road transactions made by the two Ministers.

sections.label: Actual and potential conflict defined
sections.summary: The speaker defines actual conflict as having an interest and making a decision, and potential conflict as possibly making one.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Actual conflict – I think I am glad to hear Assoc Prof Lim and others agree that there is no actual conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But just so that we understand what it means, actual conflict is, you have an interest and you make a decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Potential conflict, as I explained, arises when you have an interest and you may potentially make a decision.

sections.label: Perceived conflict of interest
sections.summary: The speaker says perceived conflict means being in conflict and breaching the Ministerial code if others perceive conflict.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If there is no actual conflict nor potential conflict, what does perceived conflict in this context mean?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It seems to me, in essence, the essence of Assoc Prof Jamus Lim's questions and some of the other questions, including Ms Sylvia Lim's questions, is that if others perceive you to be in conflict, therefore, you are in conflict; and therefore, you are in breach of the Ministerial code.

sections.label: Ministerial Code of Conduct
sections.summary: The Ministerial Code of Conduct does not mean you get to absurd results.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Ministerial Code of Conduct does not mean you get to absurd results.

sections.label: Ministry transaction restriction
sections.summary: The speaker says that if you are in charge of a Ministry, you must not engage in any transaction available to public citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Strip it of all this legalese that people use, in essence, what is being said is, if you are in charge of a Ministry, you must not engage in any transaction which is available to public citizens.

sections.label: Potential conflict of interest
sections.summary: The speaker saw a potential or perceived conflict of interest, though not actual, if he remained in the chain of command.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In my mind, there was a possibility of a potential or perceived conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I did not think there was going to be any actual conflict of interest because, as I said, rentals do not come up to MinLaw.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But there is a potential conflict of interest if I remain in the chain of command.

sections.label: Senior person oversight
sections.summary: The speaker did not want to take the chance and wanted a more senior person to have a say if the matter came up.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I did not even want to take that chance.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I wanted to make sure that there was somebody more senior than me who can have a say in the matter if it came up.

sections.label: Minister's power over interest
sections.summary: The speaker says the Minister for Law, though recused from decision-making, has power over his personal interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But his personal interest is affected, can be affected by the decision of the CEO of SLA, who reports to the Minister for Law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, indirectly, the Minister for Law, although recusing himself from the decision-making process, has power over his personal interest.

sections.label: Ministers renting public bungalows
sections.summary: Questions whether ministers renting public bungalows creates a bad picture, and states Shanmugam removed himself from potential conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Because Singaporeans are already saying the Ministers are paid million-dollar salaries, the Ministers have private bungalows of their own and they still go and rent a relatively cheaper public bungalow, which are the three most prestigious bungalows in Singapore and having the Government fork out over a million dollars to reinstate the bungalows before they move in?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Do you not think that scenario conjures up a very bad picture?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And that Minister Vivian Balakrishnan is not in a conflict of interest situation; that Minister Shanmugam was in a position of potential conflict of interest and that he took steps to make sure that he removed himself from that potential conflict of interest so that no actual conflict of interest could arise or did arise.

sections.label: Bungalow management and valuations
sections.summary: States 83% of bungalows are managed by MAs and 17% by SLA, all rented at market rates, with valuations done separately from leasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Eighty-three percent of them are managed by MAs, about 17% are managed by SLA, and they are all rented out at market rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The valuations are done by the valuation department in SLA, quite distinct and separate from the leasing department, as we have explained and as we demonstrated.

sections.label: SLA and tenant cost sharing
sections.summary: States SLA puts in money if a credible tenant also puts in money, with sums around $500,000 to restore basic habitable condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, when the prospect of a tenant comes up and the tenant is prepared to offer or looks like he is a credible tenant who looks like he can offer you a decent rent, then SLA says, "I will put in the money, if the potential tenant is also prepared to put in money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And then, we can talk." The sums look large, $500,000 in round numbers, SLA says to put the building back into basic habitable condition.

sections.label: SLA rental collection timeline
sections.summary: States SLA will collect back between $500,000 and $700,000 from rental in the first two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Within the first two years, the first three years, SLA will collect back somewhere between $600,000 and $750,000 – I am getting my numbers mixed up – $500,000, $600,000, $700,000 from the rental in the first three years of rental – two to three years of rental.

sections.label: Black and white bungalow land area
sections.summary: Asks how much land the state-owned black and white bungalow portfolio sits on and how it factors into economic and social weighing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Specifically, I have asked about how much land, what is the total land area that the state-owned portfolio of black and white bungalows sit on?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: And how might these factor into the Government's weighing of both economic and social factors to determine how best to make use of this total land area and to manage the portfolio of black and white bungalows.

sections.label: Heritage land use and redevelopment
sections.summary: Describes balancing heritage settings with land use, citing one-north Rochester Commons and Seletar en bloc redevelopment, and SLA's innovative partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And you do not want to remove it from the adjacent property and use it for other purposes that do not cohere with the status and symbol of the heritage properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, in terms of the land that is used, as I have cited in my examples, I think some of them, we have broadened it, we have mixed it up with other developments so that it is sufficiently vibrant, you make up the place and have a certain theme to it, like we do at one-north at Rochester Commons, which I have cited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is not just the building itself or the property, but the setting in which it occurs, in which case, you need more land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But yet, other occasions, I have cited Seletar where you would take the view that there is minimal heritage value, probably more to be gained by combining it, en bloc, redeveloping it, as we did in Seletar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, these are the different uses that we have done in the past.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I would assure Mr Xie Yao Quan that SLA is very innovative in not just how it plans, moving forward, but also with the partnerships that it forms with the private sector to ensure that we optimise the uses not just from a pure revenue-generation perspective, but also making sure that we look at lifestyle, social uses and, in some cases, also social causes as well.

sections.label: CPIB device seizure and wrongdoing
sections.summary: Speaker asks Ministers whether CPIB seized and returned their mobile devices, and says the House concurs there was no wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Can I just confirm with both Ministers, in the course of the investigations, were your mobile devices seized by CPIB and returned at the end of investigations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And so, my take is that this House actually concurs that there is no wrongdoing, there is no corruption, there is no abuse of power.

sections.label: Two elements required
sections.summary: Two elements must come together for these to exist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Two elements must come together for these to exist.

sections.label: Actual and perceived conflict of interest
sections.summary: Passage states actual conflict of interest arises when a person's decision affects his personal interests, and removing either element dispels it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: If that person does something or exercises the powers that he has in a decision which affects his personal interests, then that is an actual conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: But once either one of these two is removed, then there is no actual conflict of interest or potential conflict of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: And as I said, that if one explains it and looks at it properly, any fair-minded person will then say if there is no potential conflict of interest or actual conflict of interest because the potential for that has been removed, a fair-minded person will then say then the perception of a perceived conflict of interest should be dispelled.

sections.label: Government conduct and integrity
sections.summary: Passage says the House's main point is whether conduct and reports were wrong or benefited anyone, as integrity is the bedrock.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The main point for this House is, our conduct, the reports, what we did, what we did not do – was there anything wrong, did we benefit in any way?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: These are relevant questions because, for this Government and Singapore, the bedrock is integrity, financial integrity.

sections.label: Black and Whites managed by MAs
sections.summary: Passage states 87% of Black and Whites are managed by professional MAs using inhouse independent valuers to assess guide rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The majority of these Black and Whites – to be precise, 87% of them – are managed by professional MAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Each time they do a transaction, they use their own inhouse, independent valuers to make that assessment as to what the guide rent ought to be.

sections.label: Phones and deleted messages
sections.summary: Passage states the speaker's phones had no relevant messages because they automatically delete, and CPIB looked through it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My phones did not have any relevant messages, because they automatically delete and the CPIB looked through it.

sections.label: Phones looked through, not seized
sections.summary: The speaker confirms phones were looked through and returned during the interview because no relevant material was found, not seized.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Just to confirm, it would be correct, for the record, to say the phones were not seized?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think what is right to confirm is that phones were looked through and since there was no relevant material, they were given back to us in the course of that interview.

sections.label: Direct negotiated rental at Ridout Road
sections.summary: The speaker asks on what basis weak market conditions were determined for using direct negotiated rental at 26 and 31 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: If I understand the Minister correctly, direct negotiated rental is taken in weak market conditions and that was why for 26 and 31 Ridout Road, that methodology was used up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: I have seen information from some media outlets which may or may not be accurate, which is why I am putting the question here, that at the relevant time, 2018 to 2019, most of the other properties on Ridout Road were actually rented out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: So, on what basis was the determination made that market conditions were weak, such that you had to resort to direct negotiated rental as opposed to an open bidding system?

sections.label: Ridout Road rental index figure
sections.summary: The speaker cites URA's rental index and Senior Minister Teo's report showing Ridout Road was at 71% at the material time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think that tells you what the rental index was for URA as a whole.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And in addition, specifically on Ridout Road, you will see from Senior Minister Teo's report, one of the annexes, that at the material time, it was at 71%.

sections.label: No secret property list
sections.summary: The speaker says the reason a property is not on SPIO is not confidentiality, and there is no secret list of properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is not the reason why it is not on SPIO, and I think if the Member has heard the subsequent debate that we have had on this, on the list of properties, how it is accessed and so on, there is nothing confidential about this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is no secret list of properties that only certain people can rent.

sections.label: Black and Whites not on SPIO
sections.summary: The speaker says available Black and Whites would be known by the MA and advertised widely, so not listing on SPIO is not for transparency reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: All the Black and Whites, in this case, available for renting would be something known by the MA and they would want that advertised as much as they can through their networks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, the purpose of not listing it on SPIO is not for transparency reasons, Mr Leon Perera.

sections.label: Minister Shanmugam recused himself properly
sections.summary: The speaker says Minister Shanmugam handled himself and recused himself properly, and asks leave to take time answering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: On Mr Murali's first question, I think that the Ministers, and Minister Shanmugam in this particular case, handled himself and recused himself properly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: So, I have no difficulty with what he did.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One about inequality and the other about empathy.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it goes back to the point that Mr Pritam Singh referred to as optics as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: With your leave, Sir, I would like to take some time in answering this question because this is quite important.

sections.label: Taxing the wealthy fairly
sections.summary: The speaker says taxes must be set right, notes top 10% of personal income taxpayers provide 80% of revenue, and says he paid over $2 million in taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If you do not tax enough, it would not be a fair system.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, you have to get it just right and, in Singapore, the top 10% of personal income taxpayers account for, I believe, 80% of our total personal income tax revenue, and those at the lower 20% receive about $4 in benefits for every tax dollar they pay.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, in Singapore, those who are wealthier must understand Singapore is a small place, we sink or swim together, and they need to contribute, pay more taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Personally, based just on the two, three years' income, between 2005 and 2007, before I became a Minister, I probably paid more than $2 million in taxes and, rightfully so.

sections.label: Not penalising successful people
sections.summary: The speaker says other workable suggestions are welcome, but people who do well should not be penalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of course, if there are other good workable suggestions on how we can do better, that will be good, but we should not penalise people who do well.

sections.label: Wealthy man built HDB homes
sections.summary: The passage states that staying there and his wealth did not stop him from feeling the plight of Singaporeans without homes and building HDB homes for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Staying there and his wealth did not prevent him from feeling the plight of Singaporeans who had no homes to live in and doing his utmost to solve their problems by building HDB homes for them.

sections.label: Clean wage policy and rentals
sections.summary: After moving to a clean wage policy, Black and Whites and other state-owned properties were made available to anyone, with rentals set by the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When we moved to a clean wage policy, these Black and Whites and other state-owned properties were made available to anyone and the rentals were determined by the market.

sections.label: Service not tied to residence
sections.summary: The speaker says a person's ability to serve should not depend on where he lives or how poor or rich he is.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The point I am making is, a person's ability to serve should not depend on where he lives or how poor or rich he is.

sections.label: Buying family home, paying rental
sections.summary: The speaker says this was how he was able to buy his family home and pay the rental for 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I explained, this was how I was able to buy my family home and pay the rental for 26 Ridout Road.

sections.label: 35 years serving Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker says serving Singapore is a privilege and has done so for 35 years, 20 as a backbencher and 15 as a Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a privilege, a privilege to serve Singapore, Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have done this now for 35 years – 20 years as a backbencher and 15 years as a Minister.

sections.label: Homes lived in by speaker
sections.summary: The speaker says residents judge him by his heart and commitment, and lists HDB flats, condominium, semi-detached, bungalows and GCBs he has lived in before 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My residents judge me by my heart and my commitment to serve, not by how much I earn and where I live.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have lived in an HDB flat – a rental flat, 3-room flat, 5-room flat – condominium, semi-detached, bungalows, GCBs, before I moved to 26 Ridout Road.

sections.label: Living at Ridout Road bungalow
sections.summary: The speaker says his residence has not affected his service, his previous lawyer earnings pay the rental, and he put his heart into his duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I do not think where I stay or stayed has affected whether I have been able to serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And now, I have chosen to live in a bungalow in Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I said, the money that I made in my previous job as a lawyer is essentially paying for the rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It does not change my empathy any bit from when I was living in the GCB or the previous houses.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I was asked to come forward and serve.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I could have said no and carried on with my legal career.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I felt that if the Prime Minister wanted me on his team, I had something to contribute, I could make a bigger contribution to Singapore in that way.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is for others to decide if I have measured up as a Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But in good conscience, I can say, I have put my heart and soul into it and carried out my duties to the best of my ability.

sections.label: Amortised $172,000 to $2,000
sections.summary: The speaker's second question concerns the $172,000 amount amortised to $2,000 for 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My second question has to do with the $172,000 amount that was amortised to $2,000 – this is a little bit technical – for 26 Ridout Road.

sections.label: Land clearance cost calculation
sections.summary: The speaker's second question concerns the $172,000 land clearance cost, which his calculations put closer to $4,000 over four years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: My second question has to do with the land clearance cost of $172,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: At least based on my independent calculations for the extended rental period of four years, it comes up to something closer to $4,000, rather than $2,000.

sections.label: Rental basis and land cost
sections.summary: The speaker says the 26 Ridout Road rental was on a 3+3+3 basis, with land cost amortised with imputed interest over nine years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The rental at 26 Ridout Road was granted on the basis of a 3+3+3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, what was done was to take the land cost and amortise it with an imputed interest across a nine-year period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In the case of 26 and 31 Ridout Road, the amount spent for preparatory works amounted to 2.2 years of their rental respectively.

sections.label: Dalvey Estate and Ridout Road rent
sections.summary: A question asks why SLA imposed $2,000 more rental for extra land at 26 Ridout Road when a Dalvey Estate tenant gave up land.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Senior Minister Teo quoted the example of Dalvey Estate, that the Dalvey Estate tenant was willing to let SLA take back the land and reduce the size of his unit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: So, why, in the case of 26 Ridout Road, did SLA actually impose $2,000 more on the rental for the extra land?

sections.label: 31 Ridout Road rent discount
sections.summary: The average rent is $29.60 and 31 Ridout Road is $23.05, a 22% discount, plus $570,000 spent to upgrade it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The average rent is $29.60, 31 Ridout Road is $23.05, so, that is a 22% discount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: On top of that, you are spending $570,000 to upgrade 31 Ridout Road.

sections.label: Ridout Road assessed in the round
sections.summary: The assessment is taken in the round, and for Ridout Road the period is slightly less than 2.2 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But otherwise, it is taken in the round and assessed together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And if we take Ridout Road as an example, 2.2 years as Mr Leong Mun Wai has said, I think it is slightly less than that.

sections.label: Tenant improvements and occupancy
sections.summary: The tenant offers $400,000 to $500,000 of improvements for 3+3+3 years, with 71% occupancy at that point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so, when we do that, we look at the amount of time it takes for the recovery versus the improvements that this tenant is offering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: This tenant is offering to come in with $400,000 to $500,000 worth of improvements, asking for 3+3+3 years, what is a reasonable commercial landlord going to do in that situation in the context of the market that you have seen?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think I have sent round the chart.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And, earlier on, to Mr Leon Perera's question, it is a 71% occupancy at that point of time.

sections.label: 31 Ridout Road guide rent
sections.summary: The guide rent for 31 Ridout Road was determined by an MA and valuer, and the offer is not below it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But Mr Leong, the guide rent for 31 Ridout Road is determined based on the market methodologies that I have outlined earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They were, in fact, determined, in this case, by an MA and the valuer and they cohere with what the guide rent is and the offer is not below the guide rent which, by the way, is a key consideration for SLA.

sections.label: Ministers' clean wage
sections.summary: Ministers in Singapore are paid a clean wage, described as realistic, competitive but clean.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Ministers in Singapore are paid a clean wage – realistic, competitive but clean wage.

sections.label: CPIB formal investigation ordered
sections.summary: The speaker tasked CPIB to conduct a formal investigation to establish definitively if there was any corruption or wrongdoing.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: However, after SLA's statement on 12 May, the issue continued to attract public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And so, when the two Ministers asked me to conduct an investigation, independent of their Ministries, I decided that notwithstanding my confidence in them and in the system, it would be best for me to task CPIB to conduct a formal investigation and to establish definitively if there was any corruption or wrongdoing.

sections.label: CPIB tasked to investigate
sections.summary: The speaker says CPIB can interview anyone necessary to establish facts and culpability, and tasked it on 17 May.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: And they can invite anybody: Ministers, officials, businessmen, ordinary Singaporeans – whoever it is necessary for them to interview in order to establish the facts and the truth and whether there is culpability.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: I tasked CPIB to look into this on 17 May.

sections.label: Teo Chee Hean broader review
sections.summary: After returning from Africa on 22 May, the speaker tasked Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean to review SLA's policies and processes.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: But I wanted these broader questions examined more thoroughly because, as Prime Minister, my duty is not just to be satisfied that, legally, there was no wrongdoing, but whether, quite apart from the law, there was any other kind of misconduct or impropriety.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: Therefore, after I returned from Africa on 22 May, COVID-19 notwithstanding, I tasked Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean to do a broader review of SLA's policies and processes to complement CPIB's investigation.

sections.label: CPIB found no wrongdoing
sections.summary: CPIB found no corruption or wrongdoing, no preferential treatment, no disclosure of privileged information, no abuse of position for personal gain.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: CPIB found no corruption or wrongdoing, no preferential treatment, no disclosure of privileged information, no abuse of position for personal gain.

sections.label: Imprecision in guide rent
sections.summary: CPIB found an imprecision in how SLA defined the guide rent for 26 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: CPIB did find an imprecision in how SLA defined the guide rent for 26 Ridout Road.

sections.label: SLA to review practices
sections.summary: SLA acknowledged CPIB's interpretation is correct and will review its practices and improve upon them.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: SLA has acknowledged that CPIB's interpretation is a correct one, and they will review their practices and improve upon them.

sections.label: Ministers retain full confidence
sections.summary: The Prime Minister says Ministers Shanmugam and Vivian Balakrishnan did nothing wrong and retain his full confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Prime Minister (Mr Lee Hsien Loong)
sentences.text: The Ministers, Minister Shanmugam and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, have done nothing wrong and they retain my full confidence.

sections.label: CPIB instructions and Teo review
sections.summary: CPIB was told to establish whether corruption or criminal offence occurred, and its conclusions were complemented by Senior Minister Teo's review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: CPIB's instructions from me were to establish whether any corruption or criminal offence had been committed, criminal wrongdoing had been committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: You cannot do that without going into all the facts of the case and, in the process of going to the facts of the case, they came to conclusions on preferential treatment, on disclosure of privileged information, on abuse of position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: And I think these are issues which are relevant to whether the Ministers complied with the Code of Conduct or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hsien Loong
sentences.text: So, I did not ask them to investigate the conduct, but they came to these conclusions and because their main focus had been the more narrow one of the legal question of criminal offence, therefore, I complemented the CPIB investigation with Senior Minister Teo's review, and he rode on what the CPIB did.

sections.label: SLA same tenant renewal rule
sections.summary: SLA considers that if the same tenant made the investments, renewals at the second and third +3 are taken in the round.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: One of the rules that SLA internally looks at and has in mind is, if it is the same tenant who made the investments renewing it at the second "+3" and the third "+3", then you would take it all in the round.

sections.label: No VIP treatment at SLA
sections.summary: The MA decides rentals with no VIP treatment, and SLA keeps no separate record of Ministers or public figures staying at state properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is the MA's discretion and whether it is the Minister or some other person trying to rent, they take the same position as you have heard Senior Minister Teo explain earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is no VIP treatment or VIP track, regardless of the identity or the profile of the tenant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you meet the guide rent, you are able to clear the profile of the right tenant that we want, in particular, if you are able to offer more capex to enhance, that is the tenant profile that we would want to seek.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I also want to pick up while I am on that, on one of the questions the Member has filed for written answer, which is on whether or not there is a record of which other Ministers and public figures stay at these state properties, the point consistent with what I have said earlier is that SLA does not maintain a separate record.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is no list of which Ministers, which Members of Parliament, which public figures are staying at state properties.

sections.label: Preferential rental at Ridout Road
sections.summary: The Minister did not answer that the package includes preferential rental treatment for 31 Ridout Road, with $23 per square metre below the lowest nearby rental.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: And finally, the Minister did not answer, and what I am trying to say is that, within the package, there is also preferential rental treatment for 31 Ridout Road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: He answered that it is not just the average, it is also the range of rental, but if you look at Chart 2, $23 per square metre is way, way below even the lowest rental in the Ridout Road vicinity.

sections.label: Spending on other properties
sections.summary: There are media examples of more than $500,000 spent on maintenance and refurbishment of other properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In fact, there are examples in the media of how we have spent this amount, more than $500,000, on the maintenance and refurbishment of other properties.

sections.label: 31 Ridout Road rent and upgrade
sections.summary: The passage states the tenant's negotiated rent condition was bad, and after $570,000 was put in to upgrade the place, rent is still charged at $23 per square metre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: No 31 Ridout Road, when the tenant negotiated for the rent, that condition was bad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: But after that, you put in $570,000 to upgrade the place, and you still charge at $23 per square metre.

sections.label: 26 Ridout Road rental increase
sections.summary: The passage states that because of improvement to the site being cleared, the rental of 26 Ridout Road was increased by $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: Because throughout the discussion today, we also say that 26 Ridout Road, because of the improvement to the site that was being cleared, so I have increased the rental of 26 Ridout Road by $2,000.

sections.label: Guide rent and market standard
sections.summary: The passage states that if there is a basis to push the guide rent up in a market-coherent way, it will be done, and properties are not let below the guide rent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And if, indeed, there is a basis to push the guide rent up in a way in which is the market standard and coheres with the market, of course, we will do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But this is the guide rent, and we follow the guide rent and, as I said earlier in my speech, we do not let properties out below the guide rent.

sections.label: AGC and CPIB findings
sections.summary: The passage states the AGC reviewed investigation papers and agreed with CPIB's findings of no offence, no further action, proper declaration, no abuse of power and no privileged information access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The AGC has reviewed the investigation papers and agreed with CPIB's findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There is no offence and no further action is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was a proper declaration and conduct by all persons involved to avoid conflicts of interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: There was also no abuse of power and no access to privileged information.

sections.label: Preparing fourth and fifth generation leaders
sections.summary: The passage states the speaker's most important task in the last half a dozen years has been helping the Prime Minister prepare the fourth generation of leadership and a system for fifth generation leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: My most important task in the last half a dozen years has been to help the Prime Minister to prepare not just the fourth generation of leadership, but also to make sure that we have a system in place that we are able to have a fifth generation of leaders coming in, having the time to learn, to be tested, and to gain the trust and support of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Sacrifices in politics and facts
sections.summary: The passage states politics entails sacrifices, the biggest challenge is bringing in the best team, and the House agreed to focus on facts and truth, not wild allegations, rumours or perceptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: All Members of this House know that coming into politics entails many sacrifices – privacy, continuous exposure to the glare of the public eye, especially in this age of social media, in their careers, in family time and not always being there to watch your kids grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: The biggest challenge we face is to continue bringing in the best team to do the best for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: I am glad that today in this House, we have agreed to focus on the facts and the truth, not just on wild allegations, rumours or perceptions, but to focus on the facts and the truth.
